Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' Mar 23, 2026: Fomento Economico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. FEMSA Completes Accelerated Share Repurchase Agreement, and Announces New Agreement

MONTERREY, Mexico, March 23, 2026 -- Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA or the Company) (NYSE: FMX; BMV: FEMSAUBD, FEMSAUB) today announces the completion of the derivative instrument known as accelerated share repurchase (ASR) that was first announced in December 2025. The Company repurchased a total of approximately 2.5 million American Depositary Shares (ADSs)1 of the Company at an average price of $104.41 per ADS, for a total amount of USD $260 million, with the final settlement and delivery expected on March 23 and 24, 2026.

Additionally, the Company today announces that it has entered a new ASR with a different financial institution in the United States of America to repurchase the Companys shares through the acquisition of ADSs. Under the terms of this new ASR agreement. FEMSA has agreed to repurchase from such financial institution an aggregate amount of up to USD $300 million of its ADSs. The ASR contemplates an initial delivery of 591,774 ADSs on March 2026.

The total number of shares ultimately repurchased under the new ASR agreement will be based on the daily volume-weighted average price of the Companys ADSs during the term of the agreement, less a discount. The final settlement of the new ASR agreement is expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2026.

Sep 09, 2026: Derek Gaskins Takes Marketing Helm at OXXO USA

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. He will report directly to CEO Jaime Longoria and oversee a wide array of functions including marketing, merchandising, foodservice, brand development, and supplier partnerships. Gaskins expressed enthusiasm for the role, stating, 'It's one of the most exciting scopes I've had in my career.'

OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' With Gaskins at the helm of marketing, OXXO USA is poised to become a serious contender in the competitive convenience store landscape.

Jun 08, 2026: Argosy Investors Pivot to Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. for Stability

Argosy Investors has recently highlighted Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FMX) as a key holding in its Q1 2026 investor letter. The letter, made available on June 8th, 2026, outlines a cautious approach toward investment amid a transformative landscape characterized by an AI capital expenditure boom.

In the letter, Argosy expressed skepticism regarding the sustainability of earnings for market participants and suppliers during this capex surge. The firm emphasized the challenge of balancing supply and demand, especially given the rapid advancement of AI technologies. As companies experience rising volumes and prices, there is a growing concern that earnings could be overstated if supply ramps up faster than anticipated. Despite these concerns, Argosy has identified Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. as a viable investment option.

Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V., a prominent global franchise bottler of Coca-Cola beverages, closed at $122.88 per share on June 5th, 2026. The company's stock has seen a modest decline of 0.19% over the past month, though it enjoyed a robust gain of 17.29% over the past year. With a market capitalization of $41.86 billion, Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. remains a significant player in the beverage industry.

Argosy Investors revealed its strategic move of selling shares in Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) to reallocate funds into Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. The firm expressed confidence in FMX's exposure to Coca-Cola, noting the synergistic benefits of expanding convenience store operations alongside increasing beverage sales in Mexico. This pivot underscores Argosy's belief in the growth potential of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. in a rapidly evolving market.

While Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. is not currently among the most popular stocks held by hedge funds, it still garners attention. The number of hedge funds holding FMX decreased from 16 to 13 in the last quarter, signaling a shift in investment strategies. Argosy Investors remains optimistic about FMX, even as it acknowledges that certain AI stocks may present greater upside potential and lower downside risk.

May 19, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Expands Operational Footprint with Strategic Investments

Mexico City, May 19, 2026. Coca-Cola FEMSA, the world's largest bottler by sales volume of the Coca-Cola System, continues to strengthen its leadership in Latin America through strategic investments that expand its production capacity, modernize its infrastructure and strengthen its operating platform in the region. The date of this announcement is 2026-05-20 12:12:26.321290.

Ian Craig, CEO of Coca-Cola FEMSA, emphasized the company's commitment to disciplined and long-term investments aimed at enhancing capabilities and ensuring consistent growth. "We are investing with discipline and a long-term vision to strengthen our capabilities and ensure consistent growth in the region, always close to our customers and consumers," Craig stated. This forward-looking approach aligns with Coca-Cola FEMSA's objective of optimizing its supply chain and better serving consumer preferences.

The investment strategy is designed to reaffirm Coca-Cola FEMSA's regional leadership and its adaptability in a competitive market. By focusing on sustainable growth, the company aims to drive a robust business model that is resilient to future challenges within Latin America. This strategic direction positions Coca-Cola FEMSA favorably as it seeks to meet the evolving demands of consumers across the region.

Coca-Cola FEMSA operates across several key markets, including Mexico, Brazil, Guatemala, Colombia, and Argentina, as well as in several Central American countries. The company boasts a significant operational scale, with over 90,000 employees and annual sales of approximately 4.2 billion unit cases through more than 2.1 million outlets. Its extensive network of 55 manufacturing plants and 256 distribution centers underscores its commitment to generating economic, social, and environmental value for stakeholders throughout the value chain.

In addition to its operational expansions, Coca-Cola FEMSA is recognized for its commitment to sustainability and corporate responsibility. The company is a member of various sustainability indices, including the Dow Jones MILA Pacific Alliance Sustainability Index and the MSCI ACWI Index, reflecting its dedication to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices. As Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to grow, its strategic investments and operational enhancements are expected to play a crucial role in solidifying its leadership position in the beverage industry across Latin America.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

May 07, 2026: Banorte Secures Title of Best Bank in Mexico Again

Grupo Financiero Banorte has been honored for the third consecutive time as the Best Bank in Mexico by Global Finance, a recognition that comes as the bank continues to excel in various performance metrics. This announcement was made on the 7th of May 2026, and it underscores Banorte's impressive growth in assets, profitability, product innovation, and customer engagement.

The awards from Global Finance are based on stringent criteria including asset growth, profitability, and strategic development, assessed by international analysts and consultants in the financial sector. Carlos Hank Gonzalez, Chairman of the Board of Directors at Banorte, expressed pride in the recognition, stating, "This acknowledgment reflects our financial strength and our commitment to delivering hyper-personalized solutions that anticipate the needs of our customers."

Banorte's recognition as the Best Bank in Mexico reinforces its position as a benchmark in the regional banking sector. The bank has made significant strides in technological transformation, enhancing its digital banking capabilities, and ensuring proximity to customers, which has been instrumental in its success. This approach not only caters to current consumer needs but also positions Banorte for future growth.

With a robust network comprising 1,223 branches, over 12,000 ATMs, and a workforce of approximately 35,176 employees, Grupo Financiero Banorte is well-equipped to maintain its competitive edge in the financial services landscape. The bank also integrates various financial services, from brokerage to asset management through Afore XXI Banorte, reinforcing its diverse offerings to both individuals and businesses.

Since its inception in 1987, Global Finance has been a leading publication in the financial sector, providing critical insights to corporate leaders and investors. The recognition of Banorte as the Best Bank in Mexico not only highlights its achievements but also sets a high standard for other financial institutions in Latin America.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

In the markets where Coca-Cola FEMSA operates, these bottles are commonly found in traditional trade outlets, including neighborhood stores, small groceries, and food-service channels, coexisting alongside one-way PET bottles and cans.

For Coca-Cola FEMSA, the returnable glass bottle is not merely a product but a strategic asset that caters to price-sensitive consumers while enhancing the company's sustainability narrative around refillable packaging. By allowing suppliers to generate one purchase order linked to a single pallet for one facility, Walmart aims to optimize inventory positioning based on customer demand. Furthermore, participation does not necessitate changes to suppliers' prepaid freight terms, and they can manage shipments directly through Walmart or approved third-party logistics providers.

The new automation systems at the Tepotzotlan facility will allow Walmart to process up to 42,000 orders per day, a vital enhancement to meet the increasing consumer demand for faster delivery times as online shopping continues to rise.

This investment comes at a time when Walmart de Mexico is also planning to open 18 new stores across various municipalities in the State of Mexico between 2026 and 2027. Currently operating over 400 units in the region and contributing approximately 33,000 jobs, Walmart de Mexico is poised to drive further economic growth while aligning with its broader regional investment strategy. May 26, 2026: Walmart's New Prepaid Consolidation Program Aims to Boost Delivery Efficiency

Walmart has introduced a program designed to streamline inbound supplier logistics, according to a news release on Tuesday. The initiative, called the Prepaid Consolidation Program, aims to accelerate product delivery to shelves and customers. The rollout of this program will commence on 26th May 2026.

The Prepaid Consolidation Program allows suppliers to send items under a single national purchase order to one location, rather than dispatching multiple individual orders to various facilities. This consolidation enables Walmart to improve transportation efficiency by redistributing inventory across its 42 regional distribution centers.

The phased rollout will involve supplier participation based on volume alignment and capacity expansion, as stated by Walmart. Suppliers interested in participating can reach out to Walmart or to a designated provider to check their eligibility. The initiative is expected to enhance inventory replenishment accuracy, reduce variability, and support improved in-stock rates at Walmart stores.

Mike Gray, senior vice president of Supply Chain at Walmart U.S., emphasized the company's focus on simplifying and expediting the supply chain for suppliers while ensuring product availability for customers. He noted that enhancing first-mile capabilities reduces complexity and keeps goods moving, ultimately delivering more value.

The program is designed to address existing efficiency issues faced by suppliers, who typically must create individual purchase orders and manage multiple shipments. By allowing suppliers to generate one purchase order linked to a single pallet for one facility, Walmart aims to optimize inventory positioning based on customer demand. Furthermore, participation does not necessitate changes to suppliers' prepaid freight terms, and they can manage shipments directly through Walmart or approved third-party logistics providers.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Sep 09, 2026: Derek Gaskins Takes Marketing Helm at OXXO USA

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. He will report directly to CEO Jaime Longoria and oversee a wide array of functions including marketing, merchandising, foodservice, brand development, and supplier partnerships. Gaskins expressed enthusiasm for the role, stating, 'It's one of the most exciting scopes I've had in my career.'

OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' With Gaskins at the helm of marketing, OXXO USA is poised to become a serious contender in the competitive convenience store landscape.

8.1 Activities

Fomento Económico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages through its Coca-Cola FEMSA subsidiary, which operates as one of the world's largest Coca-Cola franchisees. The company also manages a vast retail network, including the OXXO convenience store chain, which dominates Mexico's retail landscape and extends into select international markets. Additionally, FEMSA operates in logistics, fuel retailing, and health sciences. The fastest-growing segments include retail, driven by the aggressive expansion of OXXO stores and digital initiatives that enhance customer convenience, as well as beverage operations in emerging markets, fueled by rising consumer demand for non-alcoholic drinks and strategic acquisitions. This diversified approach has positioned FEMSA as a resilient player in the global consumer goods sector, emphasizing innovation and sustainability. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 5th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Sep 09, 2026: Derek Gaskins Takes Marketing Helm at OXXO USA

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. He will report directly to CEO Jaime Longoria and oversee a wide array of functions including marketing, merchandising, foodservice, brand development, and supplier partnerships. Gaskins expressed enthusiasm for the role, stating, 'It's one of the most exciting scopes I've had in my career.'

OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' With Gaskins at the helm of marketing, OXXO USA is poised to become a serious contender in the competitive convenience store landscape.

Jun 08, 2026: Argosy Investors Pivot to Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. for Stability

Argosy Investors has recently highlighted Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FMX) as a key holding in its Q1 2026 investor letter. The letter, made available on June 8th, 2026, outlines a cautious approach toward investment amid a transformative landscape characterized by an AI capital expenditure boom.

In the letter, Argosy expressed skepticism regarding the sustainability of earnings for market participants and suppliers during this capex surge. The firm emphasized the challenge of balancing supply and demand, especially given the rapid advancement of AI technologies. As companies experience rising volumes and prices, there is a growing concern that earnings could be overstated if supply ramps up faster than anticipated. Despite these concerns, Argosy has identified Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. as a viable investment option.

Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V., a prominent global franchise bottler of Coca-Cola beverages, closed at $122.88 per share on June 5th, 2026. The company's stock has seen a modest decline of 0.19% over the past month, though it enjoyed a robust gain of 17.29% over the past year. With a market capitalization of $41.86 billion, Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. remains a significant player in the beverage industry.

Argosy Investors revealed its strategic move of selling shares in Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) to reallocate funds into Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. The firm expressed confidence in FMX's exposure to Coca-Cola, noting the synergistic benefits of expanding convenience store operations alongside increasing beverage sales in Mexico. This pivot underscores Argosy's belief in the growth potential of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. in a rapidly evolving market.

While Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. is not currently among the most popular stocks held by hedge funds, it still garners attention. The number of hedge funds holding FMX decreased from 16 to 13 in the last quarter, signaling a shift in investment strategies. Argosy Investors remains optimistic about FMX, even as it acknowledges that certain AI stocks may present greater upside potential and lower downside risk.

Mexico City, May 19, 2026. Coca-Cola FEMSA, the world's largest bottler by sales volume of the Coca-Cola System, continues to strengthen its leadership in Latin America through strategic investments that expand its production capacity, modernize its infrastructure and strengthen its operating platform in the region. The date of this announcement is 2026-05-20 12:12:26.321290.

Ian Craig, CEO of Coca-Cola FEMSA, emphasized the company's commitment to disciplined and long-term investments aimed at enhancing capabilities and ensuring consistent growth. "We are investing with discipline and a long-term vision to strengthen our capabilities and ensure consistent growth in the region, always close to our customers and consumers," Craig stated. This forward-looking approach aligns with Coca-Cola FEMSA's objective of optimizing its supply chain and better serving consumer preferences.

The investment strategy is designed to reaffirm Coca-Cola FEMSA's regional leadership and its adaptability in a competitive market. By focusing on sustainable growth, the company aims to drive a robust business model that is resilient to future challenges within Latin America. This strategic direction positions Coca-Cola FEMSA favorably as it seeks to meet the evolving demands of consumers across the region.

Coca-Cola FEMSA operates across several key markets, including Mexico, Brazil, Guatemala, Colombia, and Argentina, as well as in several Central American countries. The company boasts a significant operational scale, with over 90,000 employees and annual sales of approximately 4.2 billion unit cases through more than 2.1 million outlets. Its extensive network of 55 manufacturing plants and 256 distribution centers underscores its commitment to generating economic, social, and environmental value for stakeholders throughout the value chain.

In addition to its operational expansions, Coca-Cola FEMSA is recognized for its commitment to sustainability and corporate responsibility. The company is a member of various sustainability indices, including the Dow Jones MILA Pacific Alliance Sustainability Index and the MSCI ACWI Index, reflecting its dedication to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices. As Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to grow, its strategic investments and operational enhancements are expected to play a crucial role in solidifying its leadership position in the beverage industry across Latin America.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

May 07, 2026: Banorte Secures Title of Best Bank in Mexico Again

Grupo Financiero Banorte has been honored for the third consecutive time as the Best Bank in Mexico by Global Finance, a recognition that comes as the bank continues to excel in various performance metrics. This announcement was made on the 7th of May 2026, and it underscores Banorte's impressive growth in assets, profitability, product innovation, and customer engagement.

The awards from Global Finance are based on stringent criteria including asset growth, profitability, and strategic development, assessed by international analysts and consultants in the financial sector. Carlos Hank Gonzalez, Chairman of the Board of Directors at Banorte, expressed pride in the recognition, stating, "This acknowledgment reflects our financial strength and our commitment to delivering hyper-personalized solutions that anticipate the needs of our customers."

Banorte's recognition as the Best Bank in Mexico reinforces its position as a benchmark in the regional banking sector. The bank has made significant strides in technological transformation, enhancing its digital banking capabilities, and ensuring proximity to customers, which has been instrumental in its success. This approach not only caters to current consumer needs but also positions Banorte for future growth.

With a robust network comprising 1,223 branches, over 12,000 ATMs, and a workforce of approximately 35,176 employees, Grupo Financiero Banorte is well-equipped to maintain its competitive edge in the financial services landscape. The bank also integrates various financial services, from brokerage to asset management through Afore XXI Banorte, reinforcing its diverse offerings to both individuals and businesses.

Since its inception in 1987, Global Finance has been a leading publication in the financial sector, providing critical insights to corporate leaders and investors. The recognition of Banorte as the Best Bank in Mexico not only highlights its achievements but also sets a high standard for other financial institutions in Latin America.

Jul 09, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA: A Hidden Gem in Consumer Staples

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's intrinsic value-to-price (IV/P) ratio stands at 1.50, indicating that the stock may be trading below conservative intrinsic value estimates. The company's recent financial metrics reveal total revenue of approximately MXN 292.5 billion, operating income of about MXN 40.4 billion, and a net income of roughly MXN 23.0 billion. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 7 CORPORATE PROFILE

7.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Jun 16, 2026: Walmart's New Braunfels Distribution Center to Undergo $8M Automation Upgrade

Walmart is set to initiate a significant renovation of its distribution center in New Braunfels, Texas, with a budget of $8 million. The project is scheduled to commence on August 17, 2026, and is expected to be completed by September 17, 2027. This renovation phase will focus on selective demolition, the installation of new electrical systems, enhanced material-handling equipment, and upgrades to fire suppression and compressed air systems, as detailed in a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

This ongoing renovation reflects Walmart's broader strategy to automate its distribution network and optimize operational costs. The retail giant has identified automation as a crucial element in managing its primary cost drivers: inventory and labor. Earlier this year, Walmart executives highlighted that capital spending on supply chain improvements is likely to peak in the coming years, with automation accounting for a significant share of this investment. Currently, Walmart is upgrading 23 of its 42 regional distribution centers with advanced automation technology, with plans to eventually modernize all facilities in its network.

Walmart has previously indicated that automation contributes to reduced shipping costs by improving operational efficiency. Presently, more than 60% of the retailer's U.S. locations receive goods from automated distribution centers. This strategic move towards automation is designed to enhance efficiency across Walmart's supply chain, allowing the company to respond more effectively to changing market demands.

While Walmart did not provide additional details about the New Braunfels project, the investment aligns with the company's goal of streamlining its distribution processes. As Walmart continues to modernize its operations, it is likely to maintain its competitive edge in an increasingly automated retail landscape. The commitment to upgrading the New Braunfels facility underscores Walmart's focus on leveraging technology to drive growth and operational excellence.

As Walmart embarks on this $8 million renovation, stakeholders and investors will be closely monitoring the outcomes of its automation initiatives. The New Braunfels distribution center's remodel may serve as a bellwether for Walmart's future investments in technology-driven efficiencies, reinforcing the company's position as a leader in the retail sector.

Jun 15, 2026: Walmart (NYSE: WMT) Sets Sights on E-Commerce Growth with Cross-Border Shipping

Walmart Inc. (NYSE: WMT) is accelerating its global e-commerce push with a string of moves designed to expand reach and speed up fulfillment for customers worldwide. On 11th June 2026, the retail giant opened Walmart.com to customers in Mexico, granting access to hundreds of thousands of eligible items spanning apparel, home goods, electronics, and more.

Duties, taxes, and fees are displayed at checkout for cross-border orders, giving Mexican customers full pricing transparency before completing their purchases. Walmart has also confirmed plans to extend international shipping to additional markets in the future, signaling that the Mexico launch is just the first step in a broader global strategy.

On the domestic front, Walmart announced on 28th May that 30-minute-or-less delivery is now available across 33 U.S. markets, covering more than 100,000 eligible items. Products available for rapid delivery include groceries, pharmacy items, household supplies, pet food, electronics, and prescriptions, making the service broadly useful for everyday shopping needs.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Walmart reported that global e-commerce grew 26%, with Walmart U.S. e-commerce and Walmart International e-commerce growing 26% and 27% respectively. Store-fulfilled delivery has more than doubled over the past two years, with more than 36% of U.S. orders in the quarter delivered in under three hours.

The combination of rapid domestic delivery and expanding international access positions Walmart as a formidable competitor in the global e-commerce landscape, challenging pure-play online retailers on multiple fronts. With international shipping infrastructure now taking shape and domestic fulfillment networks continuing to mature, Walmart appears well-positioned to sustain its e-commerce momentum through the remainder of fiscal 2027.

Shipping and customs clearance will be managed by established international carriers to ensure reliable delivery.

To celebrate the launch, Walmart is offering a limited-time promotion for orders shipping to Mexico, including free shipping on eligible orders of $35 or more. May 26, 2026: Walmart's New Prepaid Consolidation Program Aims to Boost Delivery Efficiency

Walmart has introduced a program designed to streamline inbound supplier logistics, according to a news release on Tuesday. The initiative, called the Prepaid Consolidation Program, aims to accelerate product delivery to shelves and customers. The rollout of this program will commence on 26th May 2026.

The Prepaid Consolidation Program allows suppliers to send items under a single national purchase order to one location, rather than dispatching multiple individual orders to various facilities. This consolidation enables Walmart to improve transportation efficiency by redistributing inventory across its 42 regional distribution centers.

The phased rollout will involve supplier participation based on volume alignment and capacity expansion, as stated by Walmart. Suppliers interested in participating can reach out to Walmart or to a designated provider to check their eligibility. The initiative is expected to enhance inventory replenishment accuracy, reduce variability, and support improved in-stock rates at Walmart stores.

Mike Gray, senior vice president of Supply Chain at Walmart U.S., emphasized the company's focus on simplifying and expediting the supply chain for suppliers while ensuring product availability for customers. He noted that enhancing first-mile capabilities reduces complexity and keeps goods moving, ultimately delivering more value.

The program is designed to address existing efficiency issues faced by suppliers, who typically must create individual purchase orders and manage multiple shipments. By allowing suppliers to generate one purchase order linked to a single pallet for one facility, Walmart aims to optimize inventory positioning based on customer demand. Furthermore, participation does not necessitate changes to suppliers' prepaid freight terms, and they can manage shipments directly through Walmart or approved third-party logistics providers.

May 26, 2026: Walmart's New Prepaid Consolidation Program Aims to Boost Delivery Efficiency

Walmart has introduced a program designed to streamline inbound supplier logistics, according to a news release on Tuesday. The initiative, called the Prepaid Consolidation Program, aims to accelerate product delivery to shelves and customers. The rollout of this program will commence on 26th May 2026.

The Prepaid Consolidation Program allows suppliers to send items under a single national purchase order to one location, rather than dispatching multiple individual orders to various facilities. This consolidation enables Walmart to improve transportation efficiency by redistributing inventory across its 42 regional distribution centers.

The phased rollout will involve supplier participation based on volume alignment and capacity expansion, as stated by Walmart. Suppliers interested in participating can reach out to Walmart or to a designated provider to check their eligibility. The initiative is expected to enhance inventory replenishment accuracy, reduce variability, and support improved in-stock rates at Walmart stores.

Mike Gray, senior vice president of Supply Chain at Walmart U.S., emphasized the company's focus on simplifying and expediting the supply chain for suppliers while ensuring product availability for customers. He noted that enhancing first-mile capabilities reduces complexity and keeps goods moving, ultimately delivering more value.

The program is designed to address existing efficiency issues faced by suppliers, who typically must create individual purchase orders and manage multiple shipments. By allowing suppliers to generate one purchase order linked to a single pallet for one facility, Walmart aims to optimize inventory positioning based on customer demand. Furthermore, participation does not necessitate changes to suppliers' prepaid freight terms, and they can manage shipments directly through Walmart or approved third-party logistics providers.

Grupo Financiero Banorte, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading financial institution in Mexico, offering a comprehensive range of services including retail and commercial banking, insurance, investment banking, and asset management. As one of the country's largest banks by assets, it serves individuals, businesses, and institutions through a vast network of branches and digital platforms. The company's core activities focus on providing accessible financial solutions such as loans, deposits, credit cards, and wealth management, emphasizing innovation and customer-centric strategies. In recent years, Banorte has seen fastest-growing segments in digital banking and fintech solutions, which have expanded its online services and mobile app usage, as well as in lending to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), fueled by economic recovery and technological advancements. Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A.B. de C.V., a leading subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, operates primarily in Mexico, focusing on the manufacture, marketing, and distribution of personal care and consumer tissue products. The company's core activities encompass a wide range of essential items, including diapers, wipes, feminine hygiene products, and household tissues under well-known brands like Huggies, Kleenex, and Scott. These offerings address everyday hygiene and health needs, emphasizing quality, innovation, and sustainability. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been baby and child care products, fueled by rising consumer demand for premium, eco-friendly options, and adult incontinence solutions, driven by an aging population and increased health awareness. Additionally, the company has seen strong expansion in feminine care, supported by targeted marketing and product diversification, positioning it as a key player in Mexico's consumer goods market. It is Mexico's largest Forest products & paper company by market capitalization.

About Arca Continental

Arca Continental, SAB. de C.V. is one of the largest Coca-Cola bottlers in the world. The company produces, distributes and markets a broad portfolio of nonalcoholic beverages, including Coca-Cola trademark drinks, sparkling beverages, bottled water, sports drinks, juices and energy drinks. It also sells snacks and other food products through businesses such as Bokados.

Arca Continental serves customers across Mexico, the United States, Ecuador, Peru and Argentina. In the United States, its Coca-Cola Southwest Beverages business supplies beverages to much of Texas, as well as parts of New Mexico, Oklahoma and Arkansas.

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 23 oct (Reuters) - La bolsa mexicana avanzaba el viernes, desligada de un débil inicio de jornada de los mercados en Wall Street, mientras los inversionistas seguían de cerca los reportes de la temporada local de resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre.

El referencial índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC .MXX subía un 0.20% a 70,031.76 puntos, poco después de la apertura. En la semana, acumulaba un retorno del 1.60%, encaminado a su tercera semana consecutiva de ganancias.

Los títulos de la firma de telecomunicaciones Megacable MEGACPO.MX encabezaban las alzas del viernes, con un 1.49% más a 55.95 pesos, seguidos por los del grupo aeroportuario GAP GAPB.MX, que sumaban un 1.48% a 417.70 pesos.

(Reporte de Noé Torres)

(( noe.torres@thomsonreuters.com ;))
